name: Dorsal approach to a single central metatarsal (2 to 4)
aliases: dorsal approach to a central metatarsal
corridor: Single dorsal longitudinal incision over the involved central metatarsal, retracting the extensor digitorum longus to reach the shaft, head, or base

positioning.text: Position supine with the foot at the end of the table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the involved metatarsal and its long axis and the extensor digitorum longus tendon.

incision.text: Make the incision over the fracture site aligned with the long axis of the metatarsal.

superficial_interval.text: Protect the longitudinal veins and the dorsal digital nerves and retract the extensor digitorum longus tendon laterally.

deep_interval.text: Expose the shaft subperiosteally, or to reach a joint incise the capsule medial to the EDL tendon and, if needed, release collateral ligaments and plantarflex the toe with a mini distractor.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with dorsal veins and digital nerves, the extensor digitorum longus and brevis tendons, and the metatarsal.

structures_at_risk.text: The dorsal digital nerves and arteries and the longitudinal veins are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The dorsal digital neurovascular structures beside the extensor tendon are the danger zone.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the extensor tendon gently and protect the longitudinal veins and digital nerves.

exposure.text: Exposes the shaft, head, or base of a single central metatarsal.

limitations.text: It addresses one metatarsal at a time; multiple metatarsals need a separate multi-incision plan.

indications.text: Indicated for a fracture of a single central metatarsal (2 to 4).

closure.text: Close any joint capsule with resorbable sutures and use subcuticular resorbable sutures and nylon for skin.

complications.text: Complications include dorsal digital nerve injury and extensor tendon adhesions.

procedure_applications.condition: A single central metatarsal fracture is fixed dorsally

questions.question: How is the incision oriented for a central metatarsal fracture?
questions.answer: Over the fracture site, aligned with the long axis of the metatarsal.

questions.question: Where is the capsule incised to reach the metatarsal head?
questions.answer: Medial to the extensor digitorum longus tendon.

questions.question: Which tendon is retracted to expose the shaft?
